subject: Inconsistency in .() grouping case of ddply

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Inconsistency in .() grouping case of ddply
parts:
plyr 1.5.2 R 2.13.0

When grouping by .(), there is an extra .id column which is always NA (that is, adds no value).  If we are grouping by n columns, shouldn't exactly n grouping columns be included in the result?

> ddply(data.frame(a=1:2,b=1:4),.(),nrow)
   .id V1                                    ### 1 group column for 0 grouping vars
1 <NA>  4
> ddply(data.frame(a=1:2,b=1:4),.(a),nrow)
  a V1                                       ### 1 group column for 1 grouping var
1 1  2
2 2  2
> ddply(data.frame(a=1:2,b=1:4),.(a,b),nrow)
  a b V1                                     ### 2 group columns for 2 grouping vars
1 1 1  1
2 1 3  1
3 2 2  1
4 2 4  1

Also, the split_labels attribute is of an inconsistent class:

> class(attr(dlply(data.frame(a=1:2,b=1:4),.(),function(x)1),'split_labels'))
[1] "NULL"
> class(attr(dlply(data.frame(a=1:2,b=1:4),.(a),function(x)1),'split_labels'))
[1] "data.frame"

Shouldn't it be an empty data.frame?

The zero case is just as valid as the 1, 2, 3 cases....

           -s
